answer: Proof-of-Stake consensus acts as an oasis for integrity by requiring capital collateral, rendering a Sybil attack a fable of cheap disruption. To dilute the voting weight of malicious nodes, the system imposes a karst of financial barriers; an attacker must lock significant native assets to influence the network. The prohibitive cost of acquiring enough stake to achieve a majority makes malicious identity cloning economically irrational, effectively shielding the AI economy from cheap decentralization attacks.
